channel.title: Juan Li · Seeing Ecology
channel.description: Visual and interactive explainers of core concepts in ecology and conservation biology

item.title: Habitat fragmentation (生境破碎化)
item.description: The landscape-scale process involving both habitat loss (reduction in total area H) and habitat fragmentation per se (breaking apart of habitat while controlling for H). — Fahrig 2003, 2013, 2017 · Laurance et al. 2011 · Haddad et al. 2015 · Fletcher et al. 2018 · Damschen et al. 2019 · Gonçalves-Souza et al. 2025

item.title: Keystone species (关键种)
item.description: A species whose impact on its community or ecosystem is large, and disproportionately large relative to its abundance. — Paine 1966, 1969 · Power et al. 1996 · Estes et al. 2011

item.title: Umbrella species (伞护种)
item.description: A candidate species whose conservation is expected to confer protection to co-occurring species; actual effectiveness requires both spatial null-model and management-benefit validation. — Wilcox 1984 · Fleishman et al. 2000 · Roberge & Angelstam 2004 · Carlisle et al. 2018

item.title: Flagship species (旗舰种)
item.description: A species selected as the focus of a conservation marketing campaign based on traits that appeal to a target audience, used to rally awareness, support, and funding. — Heywood 1995 · Walpole & Leader-Williams 2002 · Veríssimo et al. 2011

item.title: Biodiversity credits (生物多样性信用)
item.description: A certificate representing a measured, evidence-based positive biodiversity outcome that is additional and durable. Frameworks differ on use; this note focuses on voluntary, non-offset credits for nature contributions. — KMGBF 2022 · 彭昀月等 2024 · Wauchope et al. 2024 · Wunder et al. 2025 · 彭昀月, 彭奎等 2026
